about.title: Temple City Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, often at businesses along Las Tunas Drive or the shopping plazas near Rosemead Boulevard, and the aftermath can feel confusing. Under California law, a property owner isn't automatically responsible just because you fell on their premises. You generally have to show they knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why what happens right after your fall matters so much. Photos of the wet floor, broken step, or uneven pavement, along with the names of any witnesses, can make a real difference later. Surveillance footage at stores and apartment complexes is often overwritten within days or weeks, so time isn't on your side. LawProactive doesn't charge you anything to get connected with an independent local attorney who understands how these claims work in Los Angeles County, including the two-year filing deadline and how comparative fault could affect your case.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, complaint histories, and other evidence to support that.

items.title: Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many Temple City businesses and apartment complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days. Sending a preservation request quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, an insurer may try to argue you weren't watching where you were walking to shrink your payout. An attorney can push back on that narrative with facts, not assumptions.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Temple City?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a public sidewalk or building, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. Missing these windows can end your ability to recover compensation, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I fell but didn't take photos right away?
items.answer: It's not ideal, but it's not necessarily fatal to your claim either. An attorney can help track down incident reports, witness statements, or surveillance video that may still exist. The sooner you reach out, the better the odds that useful evidence hasn't disappeared.

items.question: Does it matter that my fall happened at a busy Temple City shopping area?
items.answer: High-traffic locations along corridors like Las Tunas Drive or Rosemead Boulevard often have more foot traffic and more potential witnesses, which can actually help your case. These properties also tend to have more robust security camera systems, though footage retention policies vary widely by business.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no cost to you just to have a conversation about what happened.
